title: RBACv2: Snapshot validator and replay regression suite
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Build a deterministic snapshot validator and replay regression suite for RBAC v2 changes. The goal is to produce a reproducible harness that can (1) take a set of canonical permission matrix snapshots and action traces, (2) validate that RBAC policy evaluation yields expected allow/deny decisions across user roles, admin controls, SSO/SAML assertions, and service-to-service flows, and (3) replay the same traces against new RBAC engine builds while asserting exact audit log entries and metadata. This will prevent regressions that only show up in complex, multi-actor scenarios and will provide clear audit evidence for troubleshooting.

Scope notes: we treat fixture artifacts as immutable canonical snapshots ("canonical fixtures") stored in a versioned bucket. The validator will run locally and in CI. Replays must also correlate audit log lines (request ids, policy ids) so that Console tracing and incident playbooks can pinpoint divergence. We will include SAML/SSO assertion parsing tests and admin-control edge-cases (role inheritance, wildcard permissions, temporal grants, and emergency override flows).
acceptance_criteria: A snapshot validator that accepts a fixture bundle and returns pass/fail plus a diff of mismatched assertions
CI job that executes the regression suite on every RBAC engine PR with artifacts persisted for failed runs
Audit log correlation: when a test fails, the system highlights the exact audit entries and policy evaluation path that diverged
SSO/SAML assertions are exercised: nameid/attributes, group mappings, and assertion replay are covered in at least 8 test scenarios
Admin control permutations (role creation/deprecation, emergency-sudo) validated and documented in test matrix
Fixtures are stored versioned and signed; running an older fixture against a newer engine should produce a clearly labeled compatibility report

test_plan: Create 12 canonical fixture bundles covering common and edge RBAC cases: simple role grants, role inheritance, resource wildcards, temporal grants, emergency-sudo, SSO/SAML multi-tenant assertions, cross-service tokens.
Implement validator CLI with modes: dry-run (local diff), server (HTTP evaluate), and replay (stream events into engine).
Add audit-log scraper that fetches logs from logging-service for the replayed trace ids and aligns log events with expected assertions.
Add CI workflow (github action) that runs validator for every push to rbac-engine and posts a summarized failure artifact to the PR and Slack #rbac-regressions channel.
Create compatibility checker that compares fixture metadata version to engine-supported policy-version and emits WARN/ERR codes.
Document runbook and triage checklist in Confluence (link below) and add owners for triage rotations.
audit_log_correlation: For each replayed trace the harness will capture the trace-id, request-id, policy evaluation path and produced audit entries. The validator will run a 1:1 mapping between expected event lines and actual audit rows using stable keys (trace-id + user-id + timestamp window). Divergences will be output as unified diffs showing policy-rule ids and decision timestamps.
